clue.text: Something very different to have during 29?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for a wholly separate matter, quite unlike the thing just discussed
29 is the afternoon, so this is a fresh brew poured at the traditional British teatime

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about some contrasting thing one might enjoy in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 across is PIP EMMA, old signallers' slang for p.m., the afternoon; afternoon tea is a British ritual, so a second brew is what one has then.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a matter of a quite separate kind; literally it is a second serving of the brew drunk at teatime.

clue.text: Dog breeder with retainer at sixes and sevens

indicators.note: an idiom for being in total disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dog breeder and a servant are in a muddle together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog breeder' reads as one phrase, but 'Dog' alone is the definition and 'breeder' joins 'retainer' as the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish terrier breed named after the city of Aberdeen, a kind of dog.

parts.note: a place where actors are while they act, read as a location rather than an activity

explanation.definitionFit: An actor in front of the audience is on the boards, the spot where a show is given.

definitions.meaning: the back part of the foot or shoe, partnered with the underside

explanation.surface: Someone's only friend turns out to be a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' looks like 'only', but it is the underside of a foot or shoe, whose neighbour is the back part.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear of the foot sits beside its underside; as slang the word also means a contemptible man, a rotter.

parts.note: the suffix -let makes a diminutive, so a little loop or circle, here a curl of hair

explanation.definitionFit: A curl of hair is literally a little loop, the diminutive -let added to a circlet word.

parts.note: a figure below another is under it
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Someone endures something less than a full turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure or experience something unpleasant, as with an operation, is to suffer it.

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
ops is short for opera, the Latin plural of opus, a work

explanation.surface: A dismayed cry on finding that nothing functions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' is not a verb but a plural noun: musical works are opera, abbreviated to OPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of mild dismay at a small mistake.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word it is written from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written
9 across is EASTERN, abbreviated to E
a ring is a circular track or circuit

explanation.surface: Someone is heaping things on a racetrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 across is EASTERN, standing here for its abbreviation E; 'up' turns IT to TI in this down entry, and 'on' places it above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging things in rising layers is stacking or heaping them.

clue.text: Unfavourably placed a point down at tennis

definitions.meaning: in a weaker position than others
after deuce, the player trailing by one point faces the opponent's advantage

explanation.surface: A tennis player trails by one point.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis after deuce, a player one point ahead has 'advantage'; the other is, humorously, at the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in a weaker position, and plays on tennis scoring, where the leader after deuce holds advantage.

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Every one returning from the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like 'returning' but is the noun: the rear of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from the Orient comes from Asia, the lands to the east.

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Insects buzz about a girl named Perdita.
explanation.walkthrough: Perdita, a heroine of Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale, supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-winged insects form the order whose name means two wings, the true flies.

clue.text: No-one wins or loses in this lottery

definitions.text: No-one wins or loses in this

definitions.meaning: a raffle where tickets are pulled out at random

explanation.surface: A lottery in which nobody comes out ahead or behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A tied match has neither victor nor loser; a raffle in which tickets are pulled at random is also so called.

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, as a person enters a room

parts.note: gory means covered in blood
L, for learner, is the plate a novice driver displays

explanation.surface: A novice walks into a bloody scene of grandeur.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate British learner drivers carry, so it stands for a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnificence and great beauty are both senses of the word, as in the glory of a sunset.

clue.text: Sound system provided in Hawaiian islands

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: HI is the postal abbreviation of the US state of Hawaii
provided that means if

explanation.surface: A stereo supplied on the islands of Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for high fidelity, it is a home stereo for playing recorded music.

definitions.meaning: a young growth springing from a plant, which becomes a bough

explanation.surface: A local office begins by dismissing staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of branch' looks like an instruction to take the letter B; it is a new sprout on a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprout growing from a plant is the beginning of a bough; to discharge a gun is the same word as a verb.

clue.text: It's black during the auction, black

indicators.note: one piece occurs inside the span of the other

parts.note: a sale, as in an auction sale
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: A black item comes up while the auction is on.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry the word names the colour black, from the dark fur of the marten.

indicators.note: pupils is told to come first, ahead of the word for keen

parts.note: the pupils of the eye stand for the eyes
hot means eager or keen, as in hot on something

explanation.surface: Eager schoolchildren come first in the outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' suggests schoolchildren, but it is the eyes; 'first' puts them before HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance one can see, as in within range of sight, is one's view.

clue.text: To gala I wandered despite the pain

indicators.note: the letters stray from their places into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone went off to a gala despite an ache.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term for earache, from Greek ous (ear) and algos (ache).

clue.text: Mark on a list had reprimand

definitions.meaning: to check off an item with a small mark

explanation.surface: Someone was checked off a list and then told off.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a check by an item ticks it; in British slang the same phrasal verb means to scold.

parts.note: not going back to one's house but a dwelling that travels, towed behind a car

explanation.definitionFit: A mobile house towed behind a car is a dwelling that moves about; it is also a group journeying across the desert.

clue.text: Support pivot on which lever turns

definitions.meaning: a prop or point of support
the fixed point a lever rests on

explanation.surface: A support is defined as the pivot a lever moves about.
explanation.definitionFit: The point on which a lever rests is its pivot, and figuratively anything supporting an argument is its prop.

definitions.meaning: the first name and patronymic of a Soviet foreign minister, standing for his surname
short for a petrol bomb named after that minister

explanation.surface: A Soviet statesman's favourite drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet foreign minister's surname was given by Finnish soldiers to the bottle firebomb.

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, about meaning around

parts.note: a chap is a male
to nip is to pinch

explanation.surface: A man is about to steal a clerical garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'going to'; 'about' is the container signal and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of silk worn over the left arm by a priest at Mass, an item of liturgical dress.

indicators.note: the words trap the letters inside them, across the gap

explanation.surface: Christina, a climber, caught a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground-dwelling South American game bird is one of these.

clue.text: Gold repeatedly sent back by ferry

indicators.note: the letters are returned, read from right to left
the word for gold appears twice

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Gold is shipped back and forth on a ferry.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for roll-on roll-off, a ship onto which vehicles are driven, a car ferry.

clue.text: Soft long thin piece of timber

parts.note: p, for piano, means soft in music
lank means lean, long and thin

explanation.surface: A soft, slender length of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for piano, the musical direction to play softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A long flat board of wood, as on a floor, is a cut of timber.

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter, as a motor that does not start

parts.note: a canon is a priest serving a cathedral

explanation.surface: An anonymous clergyman's engine will not turn over.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for anonymous, it marks a work whose author is unknown.

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
it can stand for an unnamed thing

explanation.surface: Someone spots something starting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb; it is a noun, a small newspaper notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal entrance into a mine is the opening of a working.

clue.text: Record had been cut short for measure for dry goods

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter, as if trimmed

explanation.surface: A record of what had been cut short serves as a measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebrew unit of capacity for grain, roughly a bushel.

indicators.note: the letters have suffered a mishap and ended up out of order

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: An aggressor, one sadly forced to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enters a land by force is an assailant.

parts.note: Pip is a girl's name, short for Philippa
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A pair of women meeting after lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is old signallers' slang for p.m., when P and M were spoken as PIP and EMMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Old military signallers' alphabet for p.m., the hours after noon.

clue.text: Be feverish but take part in a heat?

definitions.meaning: to have a higher body warmth than normal
punning: to run in a qualifying race, a heat, while the heat is also warmth

explanation.surface: An athlete is unwell but still races in a qualifying round.
explanation.walkthrough: A heat is a qualifying race, so to run in one puns on running a raised body heat.
explanation.definitionFit: To be feverish is to have a raised body heat; a heat is also a race one could run.
